# ThreadSanitizer suppressions — RETAINED AS A RECORD, NOT IN USE.
#
# ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
# │ NOT REFERENCED BY ANY WORKFLOW. `.github/workflows/tsan.yml` now builds    │
# │ with an INSTRUMENTED std (`-Zbuild-std`), under which none of the          │
# │ suppressions below are needed — the false positives they cover exist only  │
# │ when std is uninstrumented. Do not wire this file back in without reading  │
# │ that workflow's header first: reintroducing it would silently narrow what  │
# │ the detector can see.                                                      │
# └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#
# It is kept because it documents a dead end precisely, and the reasoning below
# is what ruled that approach out.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTED
#
# The job cannot instrument the standard library: `-Zbuild-std` combined with
# `cargo test` is a documented, unresolved Cargo limitation
# (rust-lang/cargo#13146 — it fails to link with "duplicate lang item in crate
# `core`"). So the sanitizer sees our code but not std's internals.
#
# The consequence is specific and predictable: TSan cannot observe the
# happens-before edges inside std's pure-Rust atomic channels, so it reports
# false races there. libtest's own result channel trips this on essentially
# every run — rust-lang/rust#39608, "ThreadSanitizer detects a data race in the
# test runner". Our code appears nowhere in those stacks.
#
# What TSan *can* still see, and why the job remains worth running: it
# intercepts pthread_create / pthread_join at the libc level regardless of
# instrumentation, so the joins that `std::thread::scope` performs — the
# happens-before edges the parallel dispatch actually relies on — are visible.
# The dispatch synchronises with a plain `AtomicUsize::fetch_add` plus those
# joins, and both are in scope for the detector.
#
# RULES FOR EDITING
#
# 1. Only ever suppress *std-internal* machinery whose synchronisation TSan is
#    structurally unable to see. Never add a pattern that could match
#    `anamnesis::` — a race in our own code is the entire point of this job, and
#    suppressing one would make the job worse than not having it.
# 2. Every entry names the upstream issue justifying it.
# 3. If `-Zbuild-std` ever becomes usable with `cargo test`, delete this file
#    outright rather than pruning it: with an instrumented std none of these
#    suppressions should be necessary.

# libtest's result channel (std::sync::mpmc). The harness sends CompletedTest
# events from each test thread to the main thread; with std uninstrumented the
# channel's internal synchronisation is invisible to TSan, so the send/recv pair
# looks like a plain data race on the queue's heap block.
# rust-lang/rust#39608
race:*std::sync::mpmc*
race:*test::event*
